summary.headline: Escorts Kubota Q2 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin fell to 9.0% from 13.1% YoY on commodity inflation, despite revenue up 16.3% to INR3,231.4 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from continuing operations rose 16.3% YoY to INR3,231.4 crores, but EBITDA dropped to INR292.4 crores and margin compressed to 9.0% (13.1% a year ago, 11.2% QoQ) on commodity inflation of roughly 8-9% against about 3.5% of price increases taken so far. Net profit fell to INR255 crores from INR321.2 crores. Domestic tractor volumes were flat-to-up at 32,628 units while the industry declined about 3%, and construction equipment grew strongly. Management guided to continued margin pressure in Q3, with recovery expected from Q4 as a new price increase of about 3-3.5% takes effect from mid-November.

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Domestic volume 32,628 units vs 32,329 YoY while industry fell about 3% to roughly 2.66 lakh; market share up 48 bps. Exports fell to 1,389 units from 1,548 YoY.

segments.name: Agri Machinery (incl. non-tractor)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue INR2,690.1 crores (+10.6%); non-tractor (Agri Solutions, engines, spares and service) now 22% of segment revenue vs 17% a year ago. EBIT margin 7.8%.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Volumes 1,764 machines vs 1,146 (+54%); revenue INR536.2 crores (+58.6%); EBIT margin 7.9%, aided by operating leverage and four price increases in calendar 2026.

guidance_outlook: Tractor margins to stay under pressure in Q3 FY27 from a further 2-3% cost inflation; recovery expected from Q4 as a new price increase of about 3-3.5% takes effect mid-November (cumulative 6-7% pricing).
Management expects commodity prices to soften from Q4 but says further price increases are possible if pressure persists.
Domestic tractor industry guided to a marginal single-digit decline for FY27, implying a double-digit decline in H2; H1 industry growth was about 8%.
Construction equipment industry growth expected to moderate to high-teens in FY27; management said H2 could grow about 15-16%.
Exports expected to stay weak for the next 6 months given the existing order book; recovery more likely next fiscal year, with flat FY27 exports a good outcome.
Normal capex about INR350 crores in FY27 and about INR300 crores in FY28; greenfield project total about INR2,000 crores over 3-4 years, with INR400-450 crores already spent on land.
capex_capacity: Normal capex this fiscal about INR350 crores, broadly on track.
Greenfield project costed at about INR2,000 crores in phases: tractor factory first, then construction equipment plant, then spare parts warehouse, over 3-4 years.
Land acquisition for the greenfield project already done at roughly INR400-450 crores; construction to start next year.
Localisation of Kubota-brand tractors (using Escorts engines) and rice transplanters is on track, with launches in coming quarters.
Powertrac 4-wheel-drive product range planned for January (early Q4), targeting gaps in the 4WD segment.
Construction equipment: BLX75K backhoe loader (Kubota engine, jointly developed with Kubota Japan), F-25 25-ton and Hydra 16 Plus 16-ton cranes showcased.
demand_pricing: Industry: April-August tractor growth about 17%; September down about 18% and October down about 16-17% on high GST-cut base and El Nino monsoon (rainfall 13% deficit).
Regional: West industry down 21% in Q2; South marginally down; MP declining; North and East marginally up. Management expects the North to be flat to marginally down in H2.
Commodity inflation about 5% in Q1 rising to 8-9% by end-Q2; about 75-80% from commodities and 20% from manpower and conversion costs. Further 2-3% inflation expected in Q3.
Price actions: about 1.5% in April and about 2-2.5% in late August (3.5% total), with a further 3-3.5% from mid-November.

4WD tractors growing faster than the market (about 17-18% of industry by management estimate); 4WD volumes up about 3x over the last 6-7 months. Promaxx and Digitrac together contribute 20-23% of Farmtrac and Powertrac sales.
Construction equipment: pass-through of about 90% of inflation to customers in H1, per management; four price increases taken in calendar 2026.
Export industry up 16% in Q2 but Escorts exports fell; October exports recovered to about 500 units a month.
Inventory correction in October and expected in November ahead of Diwali/Dhanteras stock build; management acknowledged the stock correction risk.

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity headwind was there in Q2, what price hikes were taken, and how should margins evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation rose from about 5% in Q1 to 8-9% by end-Q2 against 3.5% price increases taken; a further 2-3% hits Q3 and a 3-3.5% increase follows mid-November, with the impact mainly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much industry decline is expected in H2 and what is the regional split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a marginal single-digit full-year industry decline, implying double-digit H2 decline; West and MP are the main drags, with North expected flat to marginally down.

qa_highlights.question: Will the non-tractor business margins be comparable to tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the non-tractor business is broadly comparable to tractor margins overall, with imported harvester trading lower and parts and locally made engines at good margins; non-tractor is 18% of revenue, tractors about 65%, CE about 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 22% YoY and 14% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher production to build inventory for the season (production above sales by 20-25%) increased overhead absorption; there was a one-time inventory benefit of about 1.5% that reverses in Q3; contractual manpower costs in Haryana rose 35% from April.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and greenfield plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal capex about INR350 crores this year and about INR300 crores next year; greenfield project about INR2,000 crores over 3-4 years, with INR400-450 crores already spent on land.

qa_highlights.question: What is a sustainable CE margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the current CE margin level (7.9%) to be sustained given good demand momentum, with H2 typically about 60% of annual business; four price hikes were taken in calendar 2026.

risks_watch: Tractor EBITDA margin recovery depends on the mid-November price increase sticking amid a weak industry; management has not given a firm FY28 demand view.
Commodity prices (steel and rubber) could keep rising; management says it may take further price action if pressure persists after Q4.
H2 industry decline could be deeper than guided (double-digit, with some months above 20% per an analyst's estimate); El Nino monsoon, reservoir levels and untimely North rain add risk.
Export volumes weak (down about 14-15% in H1); recovery pushed to next fiscal year.
Inventory correction in October-November could weigh on Q3 volumes and dealer stocks.
Construction equipment growth expected to moderate to high-teens in FY27 from strong recent momentum; margins depend on steel costs and price pass-through.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term tractor outlook and market-share gains, but cautious and somewhat guarded on near-term margins and H2 demand. Management declined to give FY28 guidance and repeatedly flagged uncertainty over commodity prices and the geopolitical backdrop.
